config.title: forwardRef & Exposing DOM Nodes

intro.title: forwardRef & Exposing DOM Nodes
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple React application that uses a custom button component to demonstrate how to expose its underlying DOM node to a parent component. You will learn the core concept of using forwardRef to pass a ref through a component to access a child's DOM element directly. The main technologies involved are React's forwardRef API, the useRef hook, and JSX for structuring components. This will help you understand how to manage focus, trigger animations, or integrate with third-party libraries that require direct DOM access. By the end, you'll be able to create components that can expose their internal DOM nodes to parent components in a controlled way.
intro.usecase: In real-world React applications, forwardRef is essential when you need to access DOM elements inside custom components from parent components. This pattern appears frequently in form libraries where parent forms need to focus specific input fields on validation errors, or in complex dashboards where external controls need to scroll or manipulate specific panels. Developers use forwardRef when building reusable component libraries—like custom dropdowns, modals, or data tables—where parent components need direct access to DOM nodes for measurements, animations, or imperative interactions.

objectives: Implement a custom component using forwardRef to pass a ref through to a child DOM element.
Construct a parent component that creates a ref and attaches it to a forwardRef child component.
Manipulate a child DOM node directly from a parent component by using the exposed ref.
Configure a forwardRef component to conditionally expose a DOM node or a custom imperative handle.
Integrate forwardRef with event handlers to control child DOM behavior from a parent component.
Apply forwardRef in a practical scenario to focus an input field from a parent button click.

steps.title: Import React, useRef, and forwardRef
steps.instruction: Import React, useRef, and forwardRef from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use a single import statement to bring in all three named exports from 'react'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing multiple React APIs
import React, { useState, useEffect } from 'react';
steps.seedCode: // Import React, useRef, and forwardRef from 'react'
steps.expectedOutcome: The necessary React APIs for working with refs are imported.
successCriteria: React, useRef, and forwardRef are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've imported the React APIs needed for refs.
steps.feedbackPartial: You imported some of the required APIs. Make sure to import React, useRef, and forwardRef from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are missing or incorrect. You need to import React, useRef, and forwardRef from 'react'.

steps.title: Create a Parent Component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named ParentComponent that returns an empty fragment for now.
steps.hint: Define a function or arrow function with the name ParentComponent. Inside, return an empty fragment using <> and </>.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useRef, forwardRef } from 'react';

// Create a functional component named ParentComponent that returns an empty fragment for now.
steps.expectedOutcome: A ParentComponent function is defined and returns an empty fragment.
successCriteria: ParentComponent is defined as a function or arrow function and returns an empty fragment.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've defined a component named ParentComponent that returns an empty fragment.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've created a component named ParentComponent and it returns an empty fragment.

steps.title: Initialize a useRef in ParentComponent
steps.instruction: Inside your ParentComponent, declare a ref variable using useRef and initialize it to null.
steps.hint: Call useRef with null as its initial argument and assign the result to a variable, for example: const inputRef = useRef(null);
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: creating a ref to hold a DOM reference
const myRef = useRef(null);
steps.expectedOutcome: The ParentComponent now contains a ref variable initialized to null, ready to be attached to a DOM element.
successCriteria: A ref variable is declared inside ParentComponent using useRef(null).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're calling useRef with null as the initial value inside the ParentComponent function body.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ref initialization is missing or incorrect. Remember to declare a variable using useRef(null) inside the ParentComponent.

steps.title: Create a Child Component without forwardRef
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named ChildComponent that takes props as its parameter and returns an input element.
steps.hint: Define a new component function that accepts props and returns JSX containing an <input> tag.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a ChildComponent function that returns an input element, demonstrating that ref cannot be passed as a prop to functional components by default.
successCriteria: ChildComponent is defined as a function
ChildComponent accepts props as a parameter
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your ChildComponent is a function that accepts props and returns an <input> element.
steps.feedbackWrong: Create a function called ChildComponent that takes props and returns an input element.

steps.title: Try to Pass Ref as Prop to ChildComponent
steps.instruction: In ParentComponent's JSX, render ChildComponent and try to pass the ref as a prop named 'ref'.
steps.hint: Add <ChildComponent ref={yourRefVariable} /> inside the fragment. This will demonstrate that ref doesn't work directly on functional components.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ParentComponent will attempt to pass its ref to ChildComponent, but this won't work yet because ChildComponent doesn't accept refs.
successCriteria: ChildComponent is rendered inside ParentComponent with a ref prop passed to it.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're passing the ref prop to ChildComponent inside ParentComponent's return statement.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you're rendering ChildComponent and passing the ref prop to it. The syntax should be <ChildComponent ref={inputRef} />.

steps.title: Wrap ChildComponent with forwardRef
steps.instruction: Wrap your existing ChildComponent with React.forwardRef to accept a ref as its second parameter. Keep the same component name and return the same input element.
steps.hint: Use forwardRef to create a new component that can receive a ref. The function inside forwardRef should take props and ref as parameters.
steps.expectedOutcome: ChildComponent is now wrapped with forwardRef and can accept a ref parameter.
successCriteria: ChildComponent is defined using forwardRef, with props and ref as parameters, returning the same input element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using forwardRef correctly and that the inner function accepts both props and ref parameters.
steps.feedbackWrong: That's not quite right. Remember to use forwardRef to wrap ChildComponent so it can accept a ref as its second parameter.

steps.title: Attach Ref to Input Element in ChildComponent
steps.instruction: Inside the forwardRef-wrapped ChildComponent, attach the ref parameter to the input element's ref attribute.
steps.hint: The forwardRef wrapper provides a second parameter 'ref' after props. Pass this ref to the input element's ref attribute.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ChildComponent now correctly forwards the ref to its internal input element, allowing the parent to access the input's DOM node.
successCriteria: The ChildComponent's forwardRef function receives a ref parameter, and that ref is passed to the input element's ref attribute.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're passing the ref parameter to the input's ref attribute inside the forwardRef-wrapped component.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ref isn't properly attached to the input element. Check that you're using the ref parameter from forwardRef and assigning it to the input's ref attribute.

steps.title: Add Button to Focus Input from Parent
steps.instruction: In the ParentComponent, add a button element with an onClick handler that calls .focus() on inputRef.current.
steps.hint: Remember that inputRef.current holds a reference to the input element inside ChildComponent. Use button's onClick to trigger focus.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: button that focuses an input
<button onClick={() => inputRef.current.focus()}>
  Focus Input
</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A button appears in the UI that, when clicked, focuses the input field inside ChildComponent.
successCriteria: Button element is added to ParentComponent's JSX
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your button's onClick handler calls .focus() on inputRef.current.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button isn't properly wired to focus the input. Check that you're calling .focus() on inputRef.current inside the onClick handler.

steps.title: Add Button to Log Input Value from Parent
steps.instruction: Add a second button inside ParentComponent that logs the current value of the input element when clicked, using inputRef.current.value.
steps.hint: Create a button element with an onClick handler that accesses inputRef.current.value and logs it to the console.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: logging a value from a ref
<button onClick={() => console.log(inputRef.current.value)}>Log Value</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A second button appears next to the 'Focus Input' button. When clicked, it logs the current text from the input field to the console.
successCriteria: ParentComponent contains a second button with an onClick handler that logs inputRef.current.value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a button, but it might not be logging the input value correctly. Make sure the onClick handler accesses inputRef.current.value and logs it.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button to log the input value is missing or not functioning. Add a button with an onClick handler that logs inputRef.current.value.

steps.title: Complete the Component Structure
steps.instruction: Add a button in ParentComponent that logs the current input value to the console when clicked.
steps.hint: Add a button element with an onClick handler that calls console.log with inputRef.current.value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ParentComponent will have a second button that logs the current value of the input field when clicked.
successCriteria: A button element with an onClick handler that logs inputRef.current.value is added to ParentComponent.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but make sure it logs the input value using inputRef.current.value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button isn't logging the input value correctly. Check that you're accessing inputRef.current.value in the onClick handler.
